item: Maximum mode starts low and climbs while the articles STORED per window rise, with writer and CPU saturation decided once per window (R178, R180)
summary: Maximum mode used to open at the ceiling (50) and cut one permit on every saturated tick (about 0.3 s); on the 18 Oct lab pass of 300 sources (3 articles each) the shipped governor made 33 pool timeouts, stored 852 of 900 articles at 46.4 art/min with a 10.8 s longest hold. The governor now starts at min(4, ceiling, learned seed) and takes one decision per WINDOW: a window is read only once it has run 240 s AND seen 100 source completions (until then the reason is 'thin'). The signal is the articles STORED per minute over the window (the pass's running stored count; R180), +1 permit when it is more than 10 % above the previous window's, one step back after a climb that fell by more than 10 %, then hold; a window that stored nothing neither climbs nor sets a baseline. Writer and CPU saturation are counted per tick and decided per window: at least half the ticks saturated takes ONE cut in place of the climb. Memory-low (halve) and loop lag (minus one) stay immediate and throw the open window and the last rate away. The collector's own bytes rate (download_rate_kbps) is logged in every window record beside the articles and is the signal only when no article count is passed; the whole-process rate, which includes wiki-dump and OSM downloads, is never the signal. The ceiling stays collect_parallelism (50): R26 is intact. Target mode and the top-bar knob are unchanged. Lab evidence (G5, same configuration, n=2 against n=1): 70.3 and 69.8 art/min, 0 pool timeouts, 900 of 900 stored, longest hold 3.9 and 4.6 s, against 46.4 for the shipped governor (+51 %; two windows closed in the measured pass and both were saturation cuts, the climb was exercised once in the warm-up pass, 4 to 5). NOT shown: convergence over hours, a machine whose best permit count is high (the simulation in osm-lane/governor-plan shows the rule climbs one permit per window and stops where a permit adds less than the margin), the field's counting noise (every lab source returns the same count). Mutants killed: cut per tick, climb on equal, no margin, no step back, step back without a climb, fold share zero, fold never, cut below one, loop lag folded, start at the ceiling, bytes rate instead of articles, thin window read, zero-article window climbs, baseline taken from an empty window, rates of two units compared, ceiling ignored, no window reset, no baseline reset.
